subject: Numeracy
title: Long and short
subtopics: Comparing two lengths side by side
Long and short in stories and songs
objectives: Children will say which of two things is long or short.
Children will line up two objects at one end to compare them.
content: Comparing the length of two objects and saying which is long and which is short, lining them up at one end.
teachingActivities: Hold objects side by side with the ends lined up on the floor; say longer and shorter with a stretching gesture; model the line-up before children try.
learnerActivities: Find long and short things, line up two objects to compare, make a long and a short snake, and sing about long and short.
resources: Lengths of rope or cloth strips
assessment: Check whether each child chooses the longer or shorter of two objects and lines up objects at one end.
expectedOutcomes: Chooses the longer or shorter of two objects.
Begins to line up objects to compare.
crossCurricular: Science: measuring with hands and body

lessons.title: Long rope, short rope
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will point to the long rope and the short rope when asked.
successCriteria: Points to the long one on request
Points to the short one on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare big and small, count to five with support and match numerals 1 to 5.
resources: A long rope and a short rope
A long cloth strip and a short strip
lessons.starter: Stretch a long rope across the mat with your arms wide and say "Long! This rope is long." Hold the short rope in one hand and say "Short."
teacherActivities: Lay the two ropes on the floor with the left ends lined up. Say "This one is long. This one is short."
Ask "Where is the long rope?" Then "Where is the short rope?"
Swap the positions so the long rope is on the other side. Ask again.
Give each child a cloth strip. Ask them to find a friend with a longer or shorter strip.
learnerActivities: Children look at both ropes and point to each when named.
Children point to the correct rope each time.
Children point and say "long" or "short".
Child compares strips with a friend and says long or short.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Lay the two ropes on the floor with the left ends lined up. Say "This one is long. This one is short." Children: Children look at both ropes and point to each when named.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where is the long rope?" Then "Where is the short rope?" Children: Children point to the correct rope each time.
Step 3. Teacher: Swap the positions so the long rope is on the other side. Ask again. Children: Children point and say "long" or "short".
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a cloth strip. Ask them to find a friend with a longer or shorter strip. Children: Child compares strips with a friend and says long or short.

practical.title: Long and short parade
steps: Give each child a strip of cloth.
Call "Long" and children hold up a strip that is long; call "Short" for short.
practical.safety: Use soft cloth strips and ropes shorter than a child’s arm span to avoid tangles; never wrap rope around a neck or limb.

differentiation.support: Offer one very long and one very short rope and put them far apart.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a third rope that is longer than both.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me the long rope.
questions.expected: Child points to the longer rope.

questions.question: Which one is short?
questions.expected: Child points to the shorter rope.

expectedOutcomes: Chooses long or short on request
Says long or short with support
lessons.conclusion: Stretch the long rope between two children and say "Long, long, long." Coil the short rope and say "Short."
lessons.homeConnection: Compare a long spoon and a short spoon or long and short shoes at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to the long rope and the short rope when asked" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A long rope and a short rope
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Long, long, long, stretch it out. Short, short, short, curl it in.

lessons.title: Line them up
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Comparing two lengths side by side
objectives: Children will line up two objects at one end to see which is longer.
successCriteria: Places two objects side by side
Lines up one end and says which is longer
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare big and small, count to five with support and match numerals 1 to 5.
resources: Sticks or rolled newspaper of different lengths
A masking tape line on the floor
lessons.starter: Show two sticks and ask "Which stick is longer? How can we be sure?" Wait for ideas, then say "We line them up at the start."
teacherActivities: Place the two sticks on the tape line with the left ends at the tape. Say "Start here."
Point to the end that goes further and say "This one is longer."
Give each pair two sticks and let them line them up.
Compare three sticks and find the longest.
learnerActivities: Children watch and look at the other ends.
Children point to the longer stick.
Pairs line up the sticks and choose the longer.
Children place all three at the line and point to the longest.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place the two sticks on the tape line with the left ends at the tape. Say "Start here." Children: Children watch and look at the other ends.
Step 2. Teacher: Point to the end that goes further and say "This one is longer." Children: Children point to the longer stick.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each pair two sticks and let them line them up. Children: Pairs line up the sticks and choose the longer.
Step 4. Teacher: Compare three sticks and find the longest. Children: Children place all three at the line and point to the longest.

practical.title: Start line comparing
steps: Lay a tape line on the floor.
Children place two sticks with one end on the line.
They point to the stick that goes further.
practical.safety: Use soft or rounded sticks, such as rolled newspaper, and make sure children do not swing them; keep the area clear.

differentiation.support: Use two objects with a very big difference and hold the start end for the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put three objects in order from shortest to longest.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where do we start?
questions.expected: At the line, with both ends together.

expectedOutcomes: Lines up objects at one end
lessons.conclusion: Gather the sticks and say "Long and short, tidy up."
lessons.homeConnection: Line up two spoons or two pencils at home and see which is longer.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "line up two objects at one end to see which is longer" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Long and short snakes
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Long and short in stories and songs
objectives: Children will make a long and a short snake from playdough and say which is longer.
successCriteria: Says which snake is long and which is short
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare big and small, count to five with support and match numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Hold a toy snake and say "Ssssss! This snake is very long. Let us make long and short snakes with playdough."
teacherActivities: Roll a long snake and a short snake on the board. Hold them up and say "long" and "short".
Let each child roll two snakes, one longer than the other.
Ask "Which is the long snake? Which is short?"
Place snakes from different children side by side and find the longest.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the words.
Child makes two snakes of different lengths.
Child points to each snake.
Children compare snakes and point to the longest.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Roll a long snake and a short snake on the board. Hold them up and say "long" and "short". Children: Children watch and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child roll two snakes, one longer than the other. Children: Child makes two snakes of different lengths.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is the long snake? Which is short?" Children: Child points to each snake.
Step 4. Teacher: Place snakes from different children side by side and find the longest. Children: Children compare snakes and point to the longest.

practical.title: Playdough snakes
steps: Give each child playdough and a tray.
Roll one long and one short snake.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic playdough; tell children not to eat it; wash hands after play and check for allergy to ingredients such as wheat.

differentiation.support: Roll the snake together hand-over-hand and compare with one other snake.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make three snakes and order them from shortest to longest.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you make a short snake?

lessons.conclusion: Put all the snakes in a line from short to long and say "A snake parade."
lessons.homeConnection: Make long and short rolls with dough, clay or mud with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a long and a short snake from playdough and say which is longer" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The long and short road
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Long and short in stories and songs
objectives: Children will use long and short while listening to a story and playing a road game.
successCriteria: Chooses a long or short road on request
Uses long or short in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare big and small, count to five with support and match numerals 1 to 5.
resources: Two strips of paper or cloth for roads (long and short)
A toy bus and a toy car
lessons.starter: Lay out two road strips, one long and one short. Say "Tunde and Amina have two roads to the market. Which one is longer?"
teacherActivities: Tell the story while moving a toy along each road. Pause on the words long and short.
Ask "Which road is shorter?" and "Which will take more time?"
Let each child drive a toy car along the long road and then the short road.
Walk along two taped roads, one long and one short, in the room.
learnerActivities: Children say "long" and "short" as the toy travels.
Children point to the roads and answer.
Child drives and says which road is long and which is short.
Children walk both and say which took more steps.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story while moving a toy along each road. Pause on the words long and short. Children: Children say "long" and "short" as the toy travels.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which road is shorter?" and "Which will take more time?" Children: Children point to the roads and answer.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child drive a toy car along the long road and then the short road. Children: Child drives and says which road is long and which is short.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk along two taped roads, one long and one short, in the room. Children: Children walk both and say which took more steps.

practical.title: Two roads
steps: Tape a long road and a short road on the floor.
Children walk each and count steps up to five.
Say which was the long road.
practical.safety: Tape roads securely; keep walkways clear; children walk one at a time.

differentiation.support: Use only the long road and say "long" while walking beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many steps for each road and say which had more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which road did Tunde take going home?

expectedOutcomes: Uses long and short in a story
lessons.conclusion: Sing "Long road, short road" and put the toy car away.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two paths in your compound and say which is longer.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use long and short while listening to a story and playing a road game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: Two roads, one long and one short
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Long road, short road, walk and sing. Long road, short road, we can go.
learnerFacing.story: Tunde and Amina went to the market. There were two roads. One road was long, long, long. One road was short, short, short. "Let us take the short road," said Amina. They walked and walked and soon they reached the market. On the way home, Tunde said, "Let us take the long road and sing." They sang all the way home.

lessons.title: Length stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Comparing two lengths side by side
objectives: Children will show they can compare lengths at three stations.
successCriteria: Chooses the longer or shorter object
Lines up two objects at one end
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare big and small, count to five with support and match numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Sing "Long, long, long" and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Which is longer?" and "Can you line them up?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child lines up objects and chooses the longer.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is longer?" and "Can you line them up?" Children: Child lines up objects and chooses the longer.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use soft items only; supervise all stations; keep playdough away from mouths.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to order three objects by length.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: chooses the longer or shorter of two objects; lines up objects at one end; uses long and short.

questions.question: Can you find a short one?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Sing the long and short song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare lengths of objects at home this week.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can compare lengths at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
